steps.title: Prepare 0.5 N NaOH solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.0 g NaOH in 50 mL distilled water to make a 0.5 N NaOH solution.

steps.title: Make 2 % calcein stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g calcein in the 0.5 N NaOH solution, adjust pH to 7.0, add 1/3 × Ringer’s solution to a final volume of 50 mL, aliquot into small tubes and store at –20 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare 1 × Ringer’s solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6.78 g NaCl, 0.216 g KCl, 0.265 g CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 1.192 g HEPES in distilled water, adjust pH to 7.0 with the 0.5 N NaOH solution, and bring the volume to 1 000 mL; solution is stable at room temperature for years.

steps.title: Prepare 1/3 × Ringer’s solution
steps.instruction: Dilute 333 mL of the 1 × Ringer’s solution with distilled water to a final volume of 1 000 mL; solution is stable at room temperature for years.

steps.title: Make 0.2 % calcein staining solution
steps.instruction: Mix 300 µL of the 2 % calcein stock with 2.7 mL 1/3 × Ringer’s solution to obtain 3.0 mL per 35 mm dish (adjust volume proportionally for more dishes); store at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare 1 N KOH solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.0 g KOH in 50 mL distilled water to make a 1 N KOH solution.

steps.title: Make 0.1 % alizarin stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.05 g alizarin red S in the 1 N KOH solution, adjust pH to 7.4, add 1/3 × Ringer’s solution to a final volume of 50 mL; store at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare 0.01 % alizarin staining solution
steps.instruction: Mix 300 µL of the 0.1 % alizarin stock with 2.7 mL 1/3 × Ringer’s solution (or distilled water) to obtain 3.0 mL per 35 mm dish; store at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Create 2 % methylcellulose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g methylcellulose (1500 cP) in 50 mL distilled water, shake vigorously for several days until fully dissolved; solution can be adjusted to 2–3 % as desired.

steps.title: Prepare tricaine anesthetic stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g tricaine (MS‑222) in 50 mL distilled water to make a 2 % stock, aliquot and store at –20 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Raise embryos to desired stage
steps.instruction: Obtain fertilized zebrafish (RW strain) or medaka (Hd‑rR strain) embryos by crossing adults and raise them to the developmental stage required for analysis.

steps.title: Set up staining dish
steps.instruction: Place up to five (maximum six) larvae in a 35 mm non‑treated plastic dish containing enough room‑temperature water (1/3 × Ringer’s solution or tap water left ≥1 day to remove chlorine).

steps.title: Transfer fish without damage
steps.instruction: Use a 3 mL transfer pipette with the tip removed to let larvae pass through and gently move them into the dish.

steps.title: Remove excess water
steps.instruction: With a regular 3 mL pipette (uncut tip), aspirate the water while slightly tilting the lid to prevent fish from jumping.

steps.title: Add calcein staining solution
steps.instruction: Immediately add 3 mL of 0.2 % calcein staining solution to the dish, cover the lid, and incubate at room temperature for 15 min.

steps.title: Discard calcein solution
steps.instruction: Remove the staining solution using a 3 mL transfer pipette.

steps.title: Wash fish three times
steps.instruction: Add ~4 mL room‑temperature water, mix gently, then remove the water with a 3 mL pipette; repeat this wash two more times (total three washes) until the yellow calcein dye disappears.

steps.title: Optional immediate imaging
steps.instruction: Fluorescent images can be captured immediately, but it is recommended to image the next day to reduce background; keep fish in water at optimal temperature and do not feed until imaging.

steps.title: Alizarin red S staining (alternative)
steps.instruction: Repeat steps A1–A5 using 3 mL of 0.01 % alizarin red S staining solution and stain for 60 min at room temperature; then perform the same three‑wash procedure as in steps A6–A8.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia for imaging
steps.instruction: For zebrafish, add 10 µL tricaine stock to 3 mL water in a new 35 mm dish; for medaka, add 3 µL 2‑phenoxyethanol to 3 mL water.

steps.title: Anesthetize individual fish
steps.instruction: Using a 3 mL transfer pipette with tip removed, move one stained fish into the anesthesia dish; wait until immobilized, adding more anesthetic if necessary (do not overdose).

steps.title: Mount fish in methylcellulose
steps.instruction: Transfer the anesthetized fish to a 35 mm glass‑base dish filled with 2 % methylcellulose solution using a tip‑removed 3 mL pipette; orient the fish as desired.

steps.title: Capture fluorescent images
steps.instruction: Using a fluorescent stereomicroscope, first photograph the whole fish with a scale bar, then acquire specific bone images by adjusting orientation and magnification; work quickly because anesthesia fades within minutes.

steps.title: Recover fish after imaging
steps.instruction: Return the fish to its original 35 mm dish with a tip‑removed 3 mL pipette; gently apply water onto the mouth and gills with a 3 cm transfer pipette to supply oxygen and remove methylcellulose; confirm recovery, cover the dish, and proceed to anesthetize the next fish.

steps.title: Post‑imaging care and re‑staining
steps.instruction: Place each fish individually in a 35 mm dish or a 6‑well plate, provide food and normal care, and re‑stain with calcein or alizarin red S after several days if longitudinal monitoring is desired.
